target: Experimental traceable summary-v2 sidecar and explicit one-shot worker
primary_semantics: Produce useful hierarchical summaries whose claims, scenes, typed atoms, omissions, and retrieval anchors remain traceable to immutable source records without changing summary-v1 or any live runtime path.
invariants: Raw records and summary-v1 remain byte unchanged.
Every source item is represented in both scene context and an atom or anchor, or is named in an explicit omission with a reason.
Every L1 detail traces to a raw message ID and every L2+ detail traces through validated child summary item IDs to raw message IDs.
Required tool, command, and file locators remain exact retrieval anchors.
Source and result identities are deterministically recomputable and sidecar persistence is append-only outside the archive root.
No scheduler, summary-v1 worker, retrieval, capsule, federation, cloud, dashboard, or automatic model path is activated.
allowed_changes: Add a strict summary-v2 result schema and bounded prompt.
Add deterministic source preparation, candidate validation, projection, and external sidecar persistence.
Add an explicit one-shot model worker and an offline candidate path.
Register the scripts with existing architecture owners and add focused tests and documentation.
prohibited_changes: Do not modify existing raw, index, or summary-v1 records.
Do not activate summary-v2 in production maintenance, retrieval, capsule, federation, cloud, or dashboard paths.
Do not silently drop source material or replace exact locators with paraphrases.
Do not overwrite or mutate a previously written sidecar.
Do not send a real archive to a model without explicit authorization for that archive.
before_after_checks: Hash summary-v1 before and after sidecar creation.
Exercise the real CLI candidate path with Chinese, Japanese, currency symbols, emoji, and spaces.
Reject silent source loss, unknown references, locator drift, source tampering, result tampering, and conflicting writes.
Run focused, related, full CLI, architecture, documentation, compilation, and diff checks.
